decisions.statement: A guard fires only where the idle span passes with no reset.
A reset restarts the whole idle span.
A reset replaces the armed fire rather than adding a fire.
A guard that fires aborts the signal the guarded fetch was given.
A guard aborts with a DOMException named TimeoutError.
The abort message opens with the token a reader matches an idle timeout by.
A stopped guard is stopped for good.
A caller that arms a guard stops that guard on the paths a response can end by.
A guarded fetch hands the guard back for the caller to reset on each chunk.
A fetch given no spec is left unguarded.
A fetch given an idle span at zero or below is left unguarded.
A fetch that throws leaves the guard stopped before the error goes on.
The timers are handed in so a test needs no wait.
A guard that has already fired arms again on a later reset.
An abort signal the caller passed in is dropped where a guard is armed.
Nothing here reads the bytes the guard is waiting for.

definition: an upstream fetch aborted where no bytes arrive for a span
